comment: The live animals journey as a trader walks it, and the code each page is made of. This is the journey map page's only hand-kept input: page names, the bands they group into, their URL paths, and the folders that make up each one. Everything about themes — which touch a page, where each stands, how many rows it carries, its wave — is derived from the backlogs. Add a page here when the journey gains one; name its folders and the themes attach themselves.

pages.name: Live animals notification list
pages.note: The biggest single change on any page: tabs, cards, real search and sort, filters, paging and glance cards.

bands.band: The opening run, in the order a trader meets it

pages.name: What are you importing?
pages.note: Design Release 2.1 also asks a new type question before a notification exists. That is a separate page — see below.

pages.name: Review your notification
pages.note: The most-touched page in the service. It is also what a trader sees when they open a notification they have already submitted.

bands.band: Opened from a page, not a step in the run

pages.name: Add the CPH number
pages.note: Journey foundation has already taken this out of the opening run. It now opens only from its row on Consignment addresses.

pages.name: Party pickers — consignor, consignee, importer, place of origin, place of destination
Add a transporter — choose a type, private, commercial

arriving.name: What are you importing?, asked before a notification exists
arriving.body: A trader chooses live animals or germinal products before anything is created, so the service knows which journey to open. It is a page in the INS front door, not in the animals journey.

arriving.name: Manage templates, name a template, Review your template, view a saved template
arriving.body: A whole template feature: create, save, view, change and use a template to start a notification.

arriving.name: Permanent address
arriving.body: Where cats, dogs and ferrets will live, one card per animal, with a same-as-destination shortcut. It is summarised on Consignment addresses and listed per animal on the review.

arriving.name: A whole germinal products journey
arriving.body: Its own list, origin, commodity pages, identification, overview, review, addresses, arrival, transporter, documents, contact, declaration and submission — with no CPH number, no permanent address and no Additional details. It adds pages beside the animals journey rather than changing it.

claims.body: The step order, where each save goes, Save and return to overview, and the Amend status bar — on every question page, the overview and the review.
Save and return to overview makes the same checks as Save and continue on every page, and no page logs a trader's own typing mistakes.

The one folder that decides, for every page, whether an answer is required to go on and whether a section is complete. Changing it changes how every page judges its own answers, without changing what any page asks.

The JavaScript enhancements held until a design question is answered: the commodity search, the CPH input, the confirmation dialog and live filtering. Each one only enhances a page that already works without it.
The INS front door: the overall dashboard, its glance cards and the Action needed, Status updated and Inspection required drill-downs. No animals journey page changes.

standing.standfirst: Every page a trader sees in the live animals notification journey, and the Design Release 2.1 themes that change it.
standing.attribution: A theme is on a page when the theme's own declared folders and the page's own folders overlap — the page's feature folder, its obligation section and the services behind it. A theme whose folders reach no single page is claimed by one of the sections above rather than dropped.
standing.sources: Themes, their rows and where each stands are read from the Design Release 2.1 backlogs: the root backlog.json plus one per split theme. The opening run's order is read from the live animals frontend on main, so a reordering there shows up here.
